brief.headline: Push for 5–10% price cut to export-parity and qualify a second source — Sayaji's finances are not public, so lean on our data and backups

priceAsk.target: ₹60–63/KG, benchmarking toward the India export unit value of 42.95 ₹/kg and the lower end of the market asking band ₹60–81/kg
priceAsk.basis: Our current ₹66.48/KG sits in the market-fair zone (₹66–73/kg typical), but export parity is 42.95 ₹/kg and the market asking band starts at ₹60/kg — there's room to move down, especially as we're their customer for ₹15.03 Cr annually and we're lining up credible alternates

paymentTermAsk.summary: Keep 30 Days After Receipt — no change needed

brief.financialLeverage: Sayaji publishes no financials, so we can't see their profit margins or how tight their cash is. What we do know: we spend ₹15.03 Cr a year with them — a meaningful order book. We already pay a market-fair price (₹66.48/KG falls in the ₹66–73/kg typical band), and we have three listed alternate producers (Tirupati, Gulshan, Sanstar) plus premium global suppliers ready to quote. That gives us real walk-away power. Because their financial health is unknown, frame the ask around ensuring supply security and price competitiveness — not a squeeze, but a fair benchmark to export parity and the lower market band.

evidence.point: We are their customer for ₹15.03 Cr a year — a significant revenue line
Our current price of ₹66.48/KG is market-fair but sits above India's export unit value
The open-market asking band for Anhydrous Dextrose IP is ₹60–81/kg, with typical deals at ₹66–73/kg — the low end is ₹60/kg
We already get their best price — ₹66.48/KG is the best we pay across any Dextrose supplier
Three listed Indian producers (Tirupati Starch, Gulshan Polyols, Sanstar) are direct alternates, plus Roquette India (₹2898.05 Cr revenue) and global majors

alternates.name: Tirupati Starch & Chemicals Ltd (a lead to qualify)
alternates.why: Listed Indore maize wet-miller making Dextrose ANHYDROUS (IV-fluid grade) — exact form match; verify IP monograph CoA before switching

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd (a lead to qualify)
alternates.why: Listed starch & polyol maker, established dextrose/sorbitol supplier — a drop-in alternate

alternates.name: Roquette India Pvt Ltd (a lead to qualify)
alternates.why: Indian arm of global starch major (₹2898.05 Cr revenue); pharma-grade dextrose, very reliable, premium supplier

risks: Sayaji's finances are not public — we can't gauge their fragility or how hard we can push without tipping them into trouble
Our ₹15.03 Cr spend is large, but if we walk and they lose it suddenly, they may not have the buffer to absorb the hit — balance firmness with not destabilising a key source
All three listed alternates are leads to qualify — none are audited, priced or approved yet; start the RFQ process now so the threat is real by the next round
We already pay the best price in our own book (0.0% gap), so Sayaji may resist further cuts — anchor the ask to export parity (42.95 ₹/kg) and the ₹60/kg market floor, not to another of our suppliers
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership and the ₹15.03 Cr of business we do together — today we'd like to talk about aligning your price to export parity and the lower market band, and about qualifying a second source to de-risk our supply.
